subject: DPA questions: retention matrix and proof-of-erasure playbook
body:
From: legal@acmehealth.com (S. Rivera, Acme Health Legal)
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions: retention matrix and proof-of-erasure playbook

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for sharing the draft DPA. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we prepare internal sign-off:

1) Retention matrix scenarios: we need explicit language for (a) live inference data, (b) ephemeral KV/cache, (c) periodic snapshots/backups, and (d) debug/incident logs. For each class we require the retention floor, maximum retention, and whether onshore copies are created. Can you provide a short matrix or table that maps Redwood's default retention to the DPA line items?

2) Proof of erasure: our auditors require a reproducible playbook that shows the steps to perform an erasure (including snapshots/backups) and what artifacts Redwood will produce as proof (e.g., wipe logs, time-stamped deletion receipts). Is the proof-of-erasure process automated? If not, can you commit to a response SLA?

3) Backups & legal hold: we need language that clarifies whether backups are included in the standard deletion window or if backups are retained longer and require separate removal steps. Also: if a customer issues a legal hold, will Redwood suspend automatic deletion across primary and backup copies?

Please see attached our suggested edit bullets (we added inline comments in Exhibit B). Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Best,
Sofia Rivera
Senior Counsel, Acme Health

---

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: legal@acmehealth.com; dpo@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions: retention matrix and proof-of-erasure playbook

Sofia — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short retention matrix and a first-pass proof-of-erasure playbook; attaching both (retention-matrix-v2.xlsx and redwood-dpa-exhibit-B-draft.pdf). Key points up front:

- Live inference data: default retention = 30 days (configurable down to 0); we can offer 0 days for PHI/regulated accounts under Private/Dedicated plans.
- Ephemeral KV/cache: by design ephemeral and not durably stored beyond the inference session; retention is measured in seconds/minutes (default: session TTL). We will add explicit wording to exclude ephemeral cache from persistent backup scope.
- Snapshots/backups: daily snapshots retained 90 days by default; we can offer a 30/90/180 tier for enterprise customers. Onshore copies are only created if customer requests onshore backup or uses Private deployment.
- Debug logs/incident traces: retained 30 days; audit logs (access logs) retained 365 days by default (can be reduced in contract).

Proof-of-erasure: our proposed playbook includes:
  1) Identification of all locations (primary buckets, snapshot indices, backup vaults, KV shards).
  2) Coordinated sweep using job-id that deletes primary records and triggers snapshot invalidation.
  3) Backup retention mark: if backups are immutable, we mark records as purged on restore paths and schedule physical deletion at next retention cycle; for onshore/escrow copies we run explicit removal jobs.
  4) Audit artifacts: deletion job logs (job-id, timestamp, operator-service), snapshot manifest noting removed record ids, and a signed deletion receipt (.pdf) generated on completion.

We propose adding an SLA: Redwood issues deletion receipts within 5 business days of a verified erasure request for standard accounts, 2 business days for Dedicated/Private.

Notes / open items:
- We cannot commit to instantaneous removal from immutable backups if a customer is on a third-party backup/escrow schedule; for those we provide documented schedules and a retention exception flow.
- Legal hold: yes, we suspend standard deletion cycles if presented a valid legal hold; we will honor a documented hold request and quarantine relevant records. We will log the hold and the hold release request.

If you want stronger guarantees (e.g., zero backups, immediate destruction across all replicas), that requires Private deployment + on-prem or escrow removal workflow; we can scope that in Exhibit B.

Ask: can you confirm which retention buckets Acme wants as contract defaults (we currently show 30/90/365 in the attached matrix)? Also let us know if the 5-business-day deletion receipt SLA is acceptable.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Head of Trust & Privacy, Redwood Inference

--Attachment stubs: retention-matrix-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-dpa-exhibit-B-draft.pdf (annotated PDF)

From: dpo@acmehealth.com (M. Tran, Acme DPO)
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions: retention matrix and proof-of-erasure playbook

Chloe,

Thank you for the detailed matrix. A few clarifications from the privacy team:

- For PHI workloads, Acme requires a contractual default of 0-day retention for live inference inputs unless explicitly enabled by Acme (opt-in). Is there a technical switch we can exercise from our tenant to enforce this, or does Redwood set at provisioning time?
- For backups: we need an explicit commitment that backups containing PHI can be identified and targeted for removal within a definable window. If backups are encrypted and stored by a third party inside Redwood's control plane, we still require Redwood to provide a deletion receipt.
- Deletion receipt SLA: 5 business days is tight for our compliance team — can you commit to 3 business days for PHI workloads on Dedicated/Private and 7 days for hosted?

We'd like the retention-matrix-v2.xlsx to include one column listing whether the item is included in backups and whether it is subject to legal hold.

Regards,
Minh Tran
Data Protection Officer, Acme Health

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: dpo@acmehealth.com, legal@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions: retention matrix and proof-of-erasure playbook

Minh / Sofia — appreciate the specificity. Quick responses and proposed contract language below; I also updated the attached matrix to add the two columns you requested ("Included in backups?" and "Legal hold applies?").

1) 0-day default for PHI: technical enforcement options:
   • Tenant-level setting at provisioning: we can set tenant retention for live inputs to 0 by default; toggling requires an admin change and an audit log.
   • API flag: a call-time header can mark the request as "non-persistent" to prevent storage across all tiers.
  Proposed clause: "For regulated data classes (including PHI), Customer may elect a 0-day retention default for live inference inputs. Redwood will implement this either at provisioning or via a customer-configurable API flag; all such changes will be recorded in audit logs."

2) Backups containing PHI: we confirm Redwood will identify backup objects containing PHI and run a targeted removal job. If backups reside with a third-party provider under Redwood's control, Redwood will still produce a deletion receipt confirming removal from the provider within the agreed SLA. Proposed clause: "Redwood will identify and remove Customer PHI from backups under Redwood control and will deliver a deletion receipt. For backups managed by third-party providers, Redwood will coordinate removal and deliver a deletion confirmation within the agreed SLA."

3) Deletion receipt SLA: we can accept the split you requested for PHI: 3 business days for Dedicated/Private and 7 business days for hosted (standard). We'll cross-check internal operational runbooks to confirm 3-day feasibility for Dedicated — cc'ing Marissa and Priyom to confirm.

Open operational items (cc'd):
- Marissa: can you confirm the current job orchestration timelines for targeted backup deletions and whether 3 business days is operationally achievable for Dedicated?
- Priyom: please confirm whether the API flag to mark requests as non-persistent is available today (dev status) and when it can be GA for regulated customers. If not available, note plan and ETA.

If Marissa and Priyom confirm feasibility, I'll update Exhibit B and send a redline for final review. Happy to hop on a short call Thursday if that helps.

Thanks,
Chloe
